STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.claim: The opposition of affluent and powerful people to prophets recurs throughout this surah, as elsewhere in the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.anchor: The opposition to prophets by the affluent and powerful is a recurrent theme in this sūrah

ASAD-NOTES:23:73/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:23:73/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:23:73/r1.claim: Muhammad calls people to a straight way, but those who deny the afterlife deviate from it.
ASAD-NOTES:23:73/r1.anchor: And, verily, thou callest them onto a straight way - (23:74) but, behold, those who will not

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p269/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p269/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p269/r2.claim: The passage rebukes the disbelievers’ carelessness, then reassures the Prophet not to lose hope: he is on the right path, they have strayed, and they will see their fate.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p269/r2.anchor: he should not lose hope because of their stubbornness and arrogance; he is on the right path and these people have deviated from it

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p269/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p269/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p269/r6.claim: The concluding challenge exposes their contradiction: they acknowledge and affirm truth, then state its opposite and go astray.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p269/r6.anchor: on the one hand, they accept and declare the truth, but then they lose their senses and state what is the opposite

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p273/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p273/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p273/r7.claim: The Prophet calls them to the straight path, which reaches their true destination, but following it requires belief in the Hereafter.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p273/r7.anchor: The straight path towards which the Prophet (sws) is calling people leads them to their actual destination

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p273/r9.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p273/r9.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p273/r9.claim: The salvation path is clear and straight; evasion stems from hearts lacking belief in the Hereafter, which inevitably leads people astray.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p273/r9.anchor: those who do not believe in the Hereafter have gone astray from the straight path.

QIRAAT-ER:23:73:6#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:23:73:6#1/r1.speaker: ibdāl|sp
QIRAAT-ER:23:73:6#1/r1.claim: Sīn replaces ṣād as a phonetic alternation between non-emphatic and emphatic sibilants, with no semantic change.
QIRAAT-ER:23:73:6#1/r1.anchor: ibdāl|sp, mutawatir: sīn replaces ṣād — phonetic alternation between emphatic and non-emphatic sibilant

QIRAAT-ER:23:73:6#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:23:73:6#2/r1.speaker: ibdāl
QIRAAT-ER:23:73:6#2/r1.claim: Ishmām blends ṣād with zāy into an intermediate pronunciation; the source attests it in Ḥamza and Khalaf.
QIRAAT-ER:23:73:6#2/r1.anchor: ibdāl, mutawatir: ishmām — blending of ṣād with zāy sound; intermediate pronunciation between ṣirāṭ and zirāṭ

ALUSI-FULL:v18p54/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p54/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p54/r1.claim: Sound minds attest that the path is straight, with no crookedness that could justify suspicion.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p54/r1.anchor: تشهد العقول السليمة باستقامته ليس فيه شائبة اعوجاج توجب الاتهام

ALUSI-FULL:v18p54/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p54/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v18p54/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari gathers the proof: the Prophet was known among them and suited to be chosen; he sought neither false distinction nor worldly payment, called only to Islam, exposed their failure to reflect and blind ancestral loyalty, and they called him mad despite manifest truth and miracles, disliked truth, and rejected the saving reminder. Al-Alusi praises this account.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p54/r2.anchor: ولقد ألزمهم عز وجل الحجة وأزاح عللهم في هذه الآيات بأن الذي أرسل إليهم رجل معروف أمره وحاله مخبور سره وعلنه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p424#3/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p424#3/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p424#3/r7.claim: The straight path to which the Prophet calls them is Islam.

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:72-73/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:72-73/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:72-73/r9.claim: Sound minds attest that the path is straight, with no deviation to justify accusing the Messenger.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:72-73/r9.anchor: تشهد العقول السليمة على استقامته لا عوج فيه

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:72-73/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:72-73/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:72-73/r10.claim: The verses eliminate grounds for denial and accusation, leaving hatred of truth or lack of discernment.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:72-73/r10.anchor: حصر أقسام ما يؤدي إلى الإنكار والاتهام

BIQAI-FULL:v5p214/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p214/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p214/r1.claim: The arguments have removed all objections; the Prophet’s call is true and ennobling, especially because it comes from the King of kings through the most devoted and noble of creation.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p214/r1.anchor: خالصة العباد وأشرف الخلق , كما قام عليه الدليل

BIQAI-FULL:v5p214/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p214/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p214/r2.claim: The Prophet’s reminder calls them, despite every refuted objection, to a straight path with no crookedness or valid flaw; sound minds attest to it, and following it reaches the goal and every honor.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p214/r2.anchor: فقال عاطفا على { آتيناهم } : { وإنك } أي مع انتفاء هذه المطاعن كلها

DURR-FULL:v6p109/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p109/r11.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p109/r11.claim: Qatada glosses the straight path as a path with no crookedness.
DURR-FULL:v6p109/r11.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {وإنك لتدعوهم إلى صراط مستقيم} قال: ما فيه: عوج

DURR-FULL:v6p109/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p109/r12.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p109/r12.claim: A reported parable says the Prophet invited a reluctant man to Islam by comparing it to following a familiar guide from a rough route onto a broad, easy road.
DURR-FULL:v6p109/r12.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {وإنك لتدعوهم إلى صراط مستقيم} قال: ما فيه: عوج

BURSEVI:v6p68#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p68#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p68#3/r1.claim: Sound minds recognize the straightness of the path Muhammad calls them to; it has no crookedness that could justify accusing him.
BURSEVI:v6p68#3/r1.anchor: تشهد العقول السلمية باستقامة لا عوج فيه يوجب اتهامهم لك

BURSEVI:v6p68#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p68#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p68#3/r5.claim: The verses show unbelievers are obstinate and refuted from every angle in their refusal to follow and listen to the Messenger.
BURSEVI:v6p68#3/r5.anchor: ثم في الآيات إخبار أن الكفار متعنتون محجوجون من كل وجه في ترك الاتباع والاستماع إلى رسول الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p151#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p151#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p151#2/r8.claim: The straight path is the religion of Islam.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p485/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p485/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p485/r4.claim: The Prophet calls them to a straight path.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p485/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p485/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p485/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas reports a dream in which two angels compare the Prophet and his people to stranded travelers whom a guide leads from barren ground to abundant gardens and water; some follow him onward and some stay.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p485/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أتاه -فيما يرى النائم-ملكان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p485/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p485/r6.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p485/r6.claim: Umar reports the Prophet saying he restrains his community from the Fire, but they rush toward it; he will meet them at the Basin and disavow those who come bearing misappropriated livestock after his message was delivered.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p485/r6.anchor: عن عمر بن الخطاب، رضي الله عنه، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إني ممسك بحجزكم: هلم عن النار، هلم عن النار،

MUQATIL:23:72-73/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:23:72-73/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:23:72-73/r4.claim: The straight path to which Muhammad calls them is Islam, without crookedness.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p127#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p127#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p127#2/r1.claim: The straight path is the religion of Islam, so the people should answer the Prophet.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p127#2/r1.anchor: وهو دين الإسلام فحقيق أن يستجيبوا لك

QURTUBI-FULL:23:73-74/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:73-74/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:73-74/r1.claim: The straight path is the upright religion.

QURTUBI-FULL:23:73-74/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:73-74/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:73-74/r2.claim: The word sirat means a road; religion is called a road because it leads to Paradise.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:73-74/r2.anchor: والصراط في اللغة الطريق فسمي الدين طريقا لأنه يؤدي إلى الجنة فهو طريق إليها

RAZI-FULL:v23p98#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p98#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p98#2/r1.claim: After exposing their position, God establishes the Messenger’s case: what proof establishes as sound is more fully straight than an ordinary road.
RAZI-FULL:v23p98#2/r1.anchor: زيف طريقة القوم أتبعه ببيان صحة ما جاء به الرسول

STUDYQURAN:23:73/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:73/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:73/r1.claim: For the straight path, the commentary refers readers to 1:6.

SULAMI:v2p37#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p37#3/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p37#3/r1.claim: The straight path is the most direct and sound route to uprightness: the path of following, whose end is disclosed through correctness and truth.
SULAMI:v2p37#3/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : أقصد الطرق ، وأسد المناهج

SULAMI:v2p37#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p37#3/r2.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p37#3/r2.claim: The Prophet leads people on paths of attainment, but only the steadfast are fit for that way: those steadfast with God, seeking no other and claiming no rank or station for themselves.
SULAMI:v2p37#3/r2.anchor: قال ابن عطاء رحمه الله : وإنك لتحملهم على مسالك الوصول ، وليس كل أحد يصلح

TABATABAI:23:73-76/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:73-76/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:73-76/r2.claim: The straight path is clear, consistent in its judgment, and carries its travelers to their intended goal; this is the nature of truth.
TABATABAI:23:73-76/r2.anchor: الصراط المستقيم هو الطريق الواضح الذي لا يختلف ولا يتخلف في حكمه وهو إيصاله سالكيه إلى الغاية المقصودة

TABATABAI:23:73-76/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:73-76/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:73-76/r3.claim: Truth is one: its parts do not contradict or conflict, and it does not fail to reach the end toward which it guides.
TABATABAI:23:73-76/r3.anchor: فإن الحق واحد لا يختلف أجزاؤه بالتناقض والتدافع ولا يتخلف في مطلوبه

TABATABAI:23:73-76/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:73-76/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:73-76/r4.claim: Since the Prophet guides to truth, he necessarily guides to the straight path; those who hate truth turn away from that path.
TABATABAI:23:73-76/r4.anchor: وإذ ذكر أن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم يهدي إلى الحق

TABRISI:23:72-77/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:72-77/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:72-77/r12.claim: The straight path is monotheism, sincere worship of God, and action according to religious law.
TABRISI:23:72-77/r12.anchor: من التوحيد وإخلاص العبادة والعمل بالشريعة

THALABI:v7p52/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p52/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p52/r8.claim: The straight path to which Muhammad calls them is Islam.
THALABI:v7p52/r8.anchor: وإنك لتدعوهم إلى صراط مستقيم وهو الإسلام.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p36#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p36#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p36#2/r1.claim: Muhammad calls the Quraysh disbelievers to Islam, the straight path.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p412/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p412/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p412/r1.claim: The straight path Muhammad calls them to is the sound religion and the road to Paradise.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p412/r1.anchor: إلى دين مستقيم، وهو الطريق إلى الجنة

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:72/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:72/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:72/r2.claim: God will reward the Prophet better for his mission; his sole aim is to call people to the straight path, Islam.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:72/r2.anchor: görevini yapmanın karşılığı olarak Allah seni daha iyisi ile ödüllendirecektir. Senin tek amacın, onları “dosdoğru bir yol”a yani İslâm’a çağırmaktır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:72/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:72/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:72/r3.claim: The Meccan idolaters strayed from the path to right belief and conduct despite the Prophet’s efforts.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:72/r3.anchor: Resûlullah’ın bütün çabalarına rağmen Mekke putperestleri doğru inanca ve yaşayışa götüren yoldan sapıyorlardı

NAHHAS:v3p119/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p119/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p119/r5.claim: The straight path is the upright religion; religion is called a path because it leads to Paradise.
NAHHAS:v3p119/r5.anchor: أي إلى دين مستقيم والصراط في اللغة الطريق فسمي الدين طريقا لأنه يؤدي إلى الجنة
